messages:
acme_dev: Hey team — hitting intermittent auth failures and timeouts on our embed calls since yesterday evening. Example request-id: req_8d3f2a9b. We tried curl and the same request sometimes 401s, sometimes times out. Token is unchanged. Error log: 

[2026-03-15T21:12:43Z] req=req_8d3f2a9b status=401 message="invalid auth token" path=/v1/embeddings host=api.redwood.example
[2026-03-15T21:13:12Z] req=req_8d3f2a9c status=504 message="upstream timeout"

Can you tell us what to collect to repro quickly?

support-bot: Thanks for the report! I've flagged this for the support queue and added tags: #auth #timeout #debug-bundle. To collect a debug bundle run `/collect-debug req_8d3f2a9b` (or ask us and we can pull server traces).

erin: Hi — sorry you're seeing this. Two quick asks so we can triage: 1) a minimal curl that reproduces (include full headers), 2) a tiny SDK snippet (py/js/go) we can run locally, and 3) if possible the exact Authorization header (redact token but keep first/last 4 chars). Will start by checking those request ids in logs.

acme_dev: Here's the curl we used (redacted):

```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTEDabcd1234" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-small","input":"test sentence"}'
```

We also ran verbose trace: `curl --trace-ascii /tmp/trace.txt` which shows intermittent TCP reset around 21:13.

maria: Thanks. Can you also include the SDK user-agent and whether you're calling via our hosted endpoint or a regional endpoint? If you're on a private/dedicated instance say so. Also one more request-id we pulled: req_8d3f2ab0 (504).

sanjeev: I'm seeing a cluster-side auth reject for req_8d3f2a9b and an upstream timeout for req_8d3f2ab0. Prob two separate causes: 401 = token validation path, 504 = backend inference pod timed out. Let's get repro scripts. Below are minimal repros you can run locally — they include explicit X-Request-Id so we can tie to logs.

Python (requests) minimal repro:
```python
import requests
import uuid

RID = 'req_8d3f2a9b-local'
headers = {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-REDACTEDabcd1234',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'User-Agent': 'acme-integration/0.1',
    'X-Request-Id': RID,
}
data = {"model": "embed-small", "input": "repro test"}
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', json=data, headers=headers, timeout=10)
print(RID, resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

Node.js (fetch) minimal repro:
```js
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
const RID = 'req_8d3f2a9b-local';
fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Authorization': 'Bearer sk-REDACTEDabcd1234',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'User-Agent': 'acme-integration/0.1',
    'X-Request-Id': RID
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'embed-small', input: 'repro test' }),
  timeout: 10000
}).then(r => r.text().then(t => console.log(RID, r.status, t))).catch(e => console.error('ERR', e));
```

Go (net/http) minimal repro:
```go
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "net/http"
  "io/ioutil"
)
func main() {
  rid := "req_8d3f2a9b-local"
  json := []byte(`{"model":"embed-small","input":"repro test"}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST", "https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings", bytes.NewBuffer(json))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer sk-REDACTEDabcd1234")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-Id", rid)
  client := &http.Client{}
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err != nil { fmt.Println("ERR", err); return }
  body, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(rid, resp.StatusCode, string(body))
}
```

acme_dev: Running the Python snippet now; attaching output: 
`req_8d3f2a9b-local 401 {"error":{"message":"invalid auth token","code":401}}`

erin: Good — that repros the 401. Can you run the Node or Go a few times to exercise duration — for the timeout case include a longer timeout (30s) and run in a loop. If you hit a 504, capture the X-Request-Id and paste it.

acme_dev: Ran loop 20x Node; saw 1x 504 with id req_8d3f2ab0-local. Attached snippet from `curl --trace-ascii` around that time showing TLS handshake then no response.

sanjeev: On our side I'm opening a tracing ticket. Two parallel investigations: 
- Auth 401: we'll validate token introspection path and recent deploys touching auth microservice. Provide the token prefix+suffix (e.g., sk-REDACTED...1234) so we can match without full key.
- 504: we'll check inference pod logs for req_8d3f2ab0-local and correlate with autoscaler events.

maria: For the debug bundle we can also grab tcpdump from your IP range — can you confirm your egress IP(s)? If you prefer we can pull server-side pcap for the time window; we'd need the request ids and the approximate minute window.

acme_dev: Egress IPs: 34.122.11.9 / 34.122.11.10. 504 happened at 2026-03-15T21:13:12Z. Token shows prefix sk-REDACTED and suffix 1234.

support-bot: Collected server traces for req_8d3f2a9b and req_8d3f2ab0. Run `/download-debug req_8d3f2a9b` to get bundle link (expires in 24h).

erin: Next steps for us: 1) we will rotate any short-lived signing keys if we see a token-introspection regression, 2) infra will review pod scale events for that minute. I'll follow up in this thread once we have logs. Meanwhile, can you run the Python snippet while piping curl with `-v` and attach both outputs? That will speed up repro verification. :thumbsup:

acme_dev: Uploading logs now, attaching trace and python stdout. Thanks — will wait for updates.

sanjeev: Adding a note — if you see 401 only from one of your hosts, try cURL from another network to rule out MITM or local proxy rewriting Authorization headers. Also verify no accidental newline characters in the token header.

erin: Thanks all — tracking as SUP-6821. Will update with findings by EOD PST.
